messages.body_plain:
Hi
that's because the environment in which rmr runs is not your local environment (we are using a cluster after all). To test your node environment as seen by rmr you can do this

detach("package:rhdfs")
values(from.dfs(mapreduce(to.dfs(1), map = function(k,v) Sys.getenv())))

The output can be long, be prepared to scroll around, or test only specific variables that you are interested in. I still think you shouldn't need rhdfs in a mapper and should just detach it before calling mapreduce and be done with it. I think I'd clarify that before spending any more time on configuring rhdfs on the nodes.

Antonio

messages.body_plain:
What is your input format? What is the return value of your function? I don't think your map function is a legal map function from an rmr2 point of view. You need to return one keyval object, that is the return value of the keyval function, you just call the function many times but return NULL, the value of a for loop expression. If you are switching from RHipe, you may be thinking of RHcollect, which as far as I can remember works by side effects. This is a more functional library as in functional programming, so the value of the map for the shuffle phase is the return value of the map function.

Antonio

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#319] KeyVal problem in rmr
messages.body_plain:
Yes, they keyval function is now vectorized so it does just that

keyvval(1:3, 1:3) generates (logically, not necessarily in the implementation) three key-value pairs.

If you are returning data.frames or matrices, what counts as a record is each row. You can mix a vector key and a data.frame value, no problem. If you pass arguments of different length (number of rows where applicable) recycling is applied. Like in keyval(1, 1:10), that means 10 key-value pairs with the same key. There is an open issue  for a feature that allows to make one vectorized keyval pair out of old fashioned singletons, to help people transitioning their code. #150

Antonio
